docs.title: Clichy
docs.text:
Clichy is an on-premise photo library built for the ECAM Brussels Distributed Systems project. It provides authenticated uploads, original/preview access, metadata extraction and exact/perceptual duplicate queries. Video processing and automatic blurry-photo detection are not implemented.

Start with local setup; Kubernetes is not needed for application development. Use testing before submitting a change, and the scripts catalogue to operate an environment.

docs.text: Need Read Understand components Architecture and application flow Understand public/private access Networking Prepare the server Kubernetes Follow a commit into Test/Production CI/CD Understand Citus and replication Databases Observe load and scale Monitoring Update an environment Deployment and migrations Investigate a failure Troubleshooting Decode a term Glossary

docs.title: Scope and academic evaluation
docs.text:
The cluster intentionally runs on one host, valtask. Configuration in Git is not proof of live operation; capture workflow runs and healthcheck output when demonstrating it.

Requirement Implementation and remaining evidence Tests, images and automatic Test deployment GitHub Actions tests/builds; GHCR SHA tags; self-hosted Test runner Production promotion and migrations Manual dispatch after Test; migrations before application rollout; GitHub environment protection depends on repository settings Sharding Test Citus: userId, 32 colocated Photo/outbox shards; one Pod, not multi-node capacity Replication CNPG: two instances and asynchronous WAL streaming; live streaming/failover must be observed separately Rolling updates and scaling Deployments and Test API/Web HPA; zero downtime and scaling require measurements Monitoring Prometheus, API/worker/CNPG metrics and Grafana dashboard; verify scrape health Isolation and ingress Namespace-specific Secrets, Redis and storage; Traefik routes UI/API; Production tunnel is configured outside Git Known gaps No tested backup/restore automation, Test refresh/anonymization or replicated Redis; all data shares one physical host

docs.title: Application and photo processing
docs.text:
What is it? React Router renders the Web application; Fastify serves HTTP and Better Auth handles email/password sessions backed by Prisma/PostgreSQL. Redis is an in-memory data store; BullMQ uses it as a durable job queue with retries, rather than as a photo cache.

Why Clichy uses it HTTP requests record work quickly, while an independent worker performs CPU-intensive image decoding and produces previews.

docs.title: Upload to completion
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
  participant U as User
  participant API as Fastify
  participant DB as PostgreSQL
  participant Q as BullMQ / Redis
  participant W as Worker
  U->>API: POST /photos
  API->>API: Validate and store original
  API->>DB: Transaction: Photo + outbox
  API-->>U: 202 Accepted / PENDING
  API->>Q: Dispatcher publishes stable job ID
  API->>DB: Mark outbox published
  Q->>W: process-photo (photoId, userId)
  W->>DB: Atomically claim photo
  W->>W: Read shared original; generate derivatives and hashes
  W->>DB: COMPLETED or FAILED

The dispatcher retries unpublished events. Queue identity makes repeated publication idempotent; worker claims prevent duplicate processing. Queue defaults are four attempts with exponential backoff from two seconds. Invalid images and missing originals fail permanently. Stale PROCESSING records are recovered after 15 minutes and stale PENDING records after 10 minutes; normal SIGTERM lets the worker close within its 120-second Kubernetes grace period.

The original is written before the transaction. A process crash in that window can leave an orphan file; there is no orphan sweeper. Files and metadata must be backed up together. Redis AOF improves persistence but is not replication or a backup of the library.

docs.title: API and storage
docs.text:
The API accepts JPEG, PNG, WebP and GIF, with a 20 MiB multipart limit and a 40-million-pixel decoder cap. Sharp creates WebP previews, Exifr reads optional EXIF, SHA-256 identifies exact duplicates, and a 64-bit DCT pHash ranks similar images by Hamming distance. These queries do not imply a complete duplicate review or blurry-photo classification UI.

Route Purpose /api/auth/* Better Auth sessions and registration GET /photos, POST /photos Owned photo list and upload GET /photos/:id Original GET /photos/:id/metadata Metadata GET /photos/:id/thumbnail/:variant Preview GET /photos/:id/duplicates, /similar Owned duplicate/similarity queries DELETE /photos/:id Owned record and file removal

The API serves health at / and metrics at /metrics. Worker exposes /live, /ready and /metrics on port 3001; readiness requires Redis. Queue/storage configuration comes from the environment schemas; API and worker must agree. The backfill command reschedules incomplete photos across the library and therefore belongs to maintenance, not healthchecking.

docs.title: Traefik and Ingress
docs.text:
What is it? A Kubernetes Ingress declares HTTP routing by host and path. Traefik is the Ingress Controller that implements those rules.

Why Clichy uses it One application endpoint routes the browser UI and API to separate internal Services without exposing databases or Redis.

flowchart LR
  Browser -->|HTTPS| Cloudflare
  Cloudflare --> Tunnel[Cloudflare Tunnel]
  Tunnel -->|HTTP port 80| Traefik
  Traefik -->|/| Web[clichy-web Service]
  Traefik -->|/api/auth and /photos| API[clichy-server Service]
  Tailnet[Private LAN / Tailscale] -->|Test host| Traefik
Environment Host Intended access Dev clichy.localhost Local Kubernetes only Test clichy-test.home.arpa Private LAN/Tailscale Production valtask.xyz Public tunnel

Base Ingress uses class traefik, entrypoint web, UI /, API /api/auth and /photos. Namespace-local ClusterIP Services expose Web, API, Redis and the environment database. /metrics is not routed publicly by this Ingress.

docs.title: Cloudflare Tunnel
docs.text:
What is it? cloudflared opens an outbound connection to Cloudflare, allowing public HTTP traffic to reach a private server without inbound home router forwarding.

Why Clichy uses it Only Production is public. Cloudflare terminates HTTPS, redirects www.valtask.xyz to valtask.xyz and forwards the canonical route to Traefik over the tunnel. DNS, redirects and tunnel settings are outside Git.

Grafana (http://valtask:3000) and Headlamp (http://valtask:4466) use separate LAN entrypoints. They must remain private. Traefik ports are not automatically bound only to Tailscale; restrict access through the host firewall and verify existing SSH access before changing rules. See server setup.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
What is it? Clichy separates browser UI, HTTP API and asynchronous image processing. PostgreSQL stores records; a filesystem stores image bytes.

Why Clichy uses it Uploads can return promptly while a separate worker processes durable work independently of HTTP requests.

flowchart LR
  Browser --> Traefik --> Web[React Web]
  Traefik --> API[Fastify API and outbox dispatcher]
  API --> DB[(PostgreSQL metadata)]
  API --> Photos[(Shared photos PVC)]
  API --> Redis[BullMQ / Redis]
  Redis --> Worker
  Worker --> DB
  Worker --> Photos
  Prometheus -. metrics .-> API
  Prometheus -. metrics .-> Worker
  Grafana --> Prometheus

Web calls the authenticated API. API and worker mount the same photo volume at /data/photos. The API writes a Photo and an outbox event in one transaction; the dispatcher publishes that event to BullMQ. Worker jobs carry photoId and userId; queries include the owner/shard key.

Component Source Responsibility Web apps/web Login, dashboard and photo UI API apps/server Authentication, uploads, photo queries and outbox dispatch Worker apps/worker Metadata, hashes and preview generation Shared packages packages/db, auth, jobs, ui Prisma, Better Auth, queue configuration and UI components

Test connects API/worker to a separate Citus database. Dev and Production use CNPG directly. Test's CNPG cluster is retained for replication exercises and does not replicate Citus. See databases.

Namespaces isolate configuration and resources on one physical K3s host. One host, one Redis instance per namespace and one Test Citus Pod remain failure domains. Additional application replicas do not remove this limitation.

docs.title: Local setup
docs.text:
What is it? Local development runs the Web, API and worker as Node processes, with PostgreSQL and Redis in Docker Compose. pnpm manages the workspace packages.

Why Clichy uses it Developers can work on the application without installing Kubernetes or accessing valtask.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Use Node.js 24, pnpm 12.8.1, Git and Docker with Compose. From the repository root:

pnpm install
pnpm db:start

pnpm install generates Varlock environment types. Compose starts PostgreSQL 18 and Redis 7.4; its password is for local use only. Do not copy production Secrets.

docs.title: Configure
docs.text:
Create these untracked .env files. The .env.schema beside each is the source of truth for required values and defaults.

apps/server/.env:

NODE_ENV=development
BETTER_AUTH_SECRET=replace-with-a-random-secret-of-at-least-32-characters
BETTER_AUTH_URL=http://localhost:3000
CORS_ORIGIN=http://localhost:5173
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres:password@localhost:5432/clichy?schema=public
PHOTO_STORAGE_PATH=./data/photos
REDIS_HOST=127.0.0.1

apps/worker/.env:

NODE_ENV=development
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres:password@localhost:5432/clichy?schema=public
PHOTO_STORAGE_PATH=../server/data/photos
REDIS_HOST=127.0.0.1

apps/web/.env:

NODE_ENV=development
VITE_SERVER_URL=http://localhost:3000

packages/db/.env:

DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres:password@localhost:5432/clichy?schema=public

API and worker must share the same database, Redis queue and resolved storage directory. Defaults are Redis port 6379, DB 0, no password/TLS and queue photo-processing. Set identical queue overrides in both services if needed. The local schemas already supply these defaults.

docs.title: Start
docs.text:
pnpm db:generate
pnpm db:migrate
pnpm dev

Open the Web URL printed by Vite (normally http://localhost:5173), sign up, then upload a small JPEG/PNG/WebP/GIF. The API listens on port 3000; the worker on 3001 for health/metrics. Expect upload status 202, then completed processing and available thumbnails. If Vite chooses another port, update CORS_ORIGIN.

Use pnpm dev:web, pnpm dev:server or pnpm dev:worker for one process. pnpm db:stop preserves Compose volumes; pnpm db:down removes containers and network, also preserving volumes. db:reset destroys the local database: it is not a setup or troubleshooting shortcut.

Workspace responsibilities: apps/web is React Router; apps/server is Fastify and the outbox dispatcher; apps/worker consumes jobs; packages/db, auth, jobs and ui hold shared database, auth, queue and UI code.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
What is it? Tests check behavior locally; type checking and builds verify workspace integration. They do not establish the health of a deployed cluster.

Why Clichy uses it CI must reject broken photo processing or incompatible changes before publishing images.

After installing and configuring, run:

pnpm check-types
pnpm --filter server test
pnpm --filter worker test
pnpm build
node --test packages/db/prisma/sharding.test.mjs infra/kubernetes/scripts/healthcheck.test.mjs

Server/worker suites use Node's test runner through tsx: storage, image processing, ownership queries/routes, outbox dispatch, metrics and job failures. Run a focused file with pnpm --filter server exec tsx --test src/image-processing.test.ts.

The shell tests mock kubectl: they exercise read-only behavior, missing components, timeouts, namespace isolation and exit codes without a cluster. To test all historical migrations plus Citus registration against the pinned image, with Docker available:

docker pull citusdata/citus:14.2.0
CLICHY_TEST_CITUS=1 node packages/db/prisma/sharding.test.mjs

This starts and removes one isolated, disposable Citus container, publishes no ports and mounts no host data. It checks clean installation, existing shards, nonempty tables, invalid metadata, absent extension and plain PostgreSQL branches. The integration case is explicitly skipped in the default offline test run.

For infrastructure changes, run bash -n on changed shell scripts, ShellCheck if installed, and kubectl kustomize infra/kubernetes/overlays/test (also prod, the database overlays, and citus when relevant). Rendering does not apply resources. Build this documentation with:

python3 -m venv /tmp/clichy-docs
/tmp/clichy-docs/bin/pip install -r docs/requirements.txt
/tmp/clichy-docs/bin/mkdocs build --strict

An upload smoke test writes application data. A healthcheck only observes state; keep these results separate when recording a demonstration.

docs.title: CI/CD
docs.text:
What is it? GitHub Actions executes workflow jobs; GHCR stores OCI container images. A self-hosted runner executes authorized deployment jobs on valtask.

Why Clichy uses it Tests and reproducible images precede deployment, with one immutable sha-<40-character-commit> tag tying migrations and images together.

flowchart TD
  Change[Push / PR / manual dispatch] --> CI[Types, tests and builds]
  CI --> Images[Build Web / API / worker images]
  Images -->|PR| End[No publication or deployment]
  Images -->|master push or dispatch| GHCR[Login and publish exact SHA tags]
  GHCR --> Test[Verify valtask and SHA; migrate; deploy Test]
  Test --> Gate{Manual dispatch with deploy_prod=true?}
  Gate -->|yes| Production[GitHub production environment; migrate; deploy same SHA]

The single source is .github/workflows/ci.yml. Pushes/PRs target master. CI uses Node 24, pnpm's frozen lockfile, type checks, server/worker tests, Citus migration integration tests in a disposable Docker container, healthcheck regression tests and builds. Packaging uses the three Dockerfiles under infra/; only master pushes or manual dispatches publish images.

Test deploys automatically after successful CI/package. Production additionally requires workflow_dispatch with deploy_prod=true, successful Test deployment and GitHub Environment production. Approval rules are repository settings, not guaranteed by the YAML. Pull requests never run on the deployment runner. Jobs serialize deployments per environment. There is no automatic rollback or end-to-end smoke-test gate.

docs.title: Runner setup
docs.text:
Register a non-root Linux runner using Settings → Actions → Runners and the registration commands/token GitHub supplies. Give it labels self-hosted, linux, install its service using the supplied svc.sh, and provide Node 24, pnpm, kubectl, Git and access to GHCR and the cluster. Do not run untrusted PR code with these credentials.

The workflow explicitly uses KUBECONFIG=/home/valatras/.kube/config. The runner account must be able to read that protected kubeconfig; a different account/path requires a deliberate workflow update. Keep mode 0600 and verify access as the actual runner account. Runner credentials are distinct from each namespace's ghcr-pull-secret.

Deployment checks the checked-out SHA, image tag and single node valtask. The database workspace is installed from that same commit. Migrations run before new application manifests; failed migrations stop deployment. See the deployment runbook for operator commands.

docs.title: PostgreSQL and Prisma
docs.text:
What is it? PostgreSQL is the relational database; Prisma supplies typed queries and versioned SQL migrations. A schema describes tables and constraints.

Why Clichy uses it Users, sessions, photo metadata and outbox events need consistent transactions. Image bytes remain on the photos volume.

Schemas and immutable migration history live in packages/db/prisma. Use prisma migrate dev locally and prisma migrate deploy for deployed environments, through the documented entry points. Never edit an applied migration or replace its history with db push.

docs.title: Citus: Test photo metadata
docs.text:
What is it? Citus extends PostgreSQL with distributed/reference tables. A distribution key selects a hash shard; colocated tables share shard placement.

Why Clichy uses it Test demonstrates logical sharding by user, keeping a photo and its processing outbox colocated. Production and Dev do not use Citus.

flowchart LR
  App[Test API and worker] --> Citus[One Citus Pod / clichy-citus-rw]
  Citus --> User[user: reference table]
  Citus --> Photo[Photo: hash userId / 32 shards]
  Citus --> Outbox[PhotoProcessingOutbox: hash userId / 32 shards]
  Photo ---|same colocation ID| Outbox
  Citus --> PVC[(One data PVC on valtask)]

The pinned citusdata/citus:14.2.0 image initializes its own extension on a fresh volume. No repository init/repair ConfigMap is needed. Migration 20261117130000_register_citus_sharding owns registration: it only acts in clichy_test, requires the extension, creates missing registrations and checks the expected layout in one transaction. Existing correct shards are left intact; incorrect existing registrations fail without automatic conversion. Future sharding changes belong in new migrations, not a second post-deploy SQL mechanism.

user is a reference table (n/t, one shard); Photo/outbox use hash(userId), 32 shards each and the same positive colocation ID. Primary/unique keys include userId; the outbox FK is (userId, photoId) -> Photo(userId, id). Photo-to-user delete is RESTRICT, outbox-to-photo delete is CASCADE; both updates are RESTRICT, since shard keys are immutable. Application jobs/queries carry userId.

This is one PostgreSQL process on one host, not multi-node scale-out or HA. The healthcheck checks layout and FKs without executing migrations. For detailed metadata inspection:

kubectl exec -i -n clichy-test deployment/clichy-citus -- \
  env PGOPTIONS='-c default_transaction_read_only=on -c statement_timeout=10000' \
  psql -X -U clichy -d clichy_test <<'SQL'
SELECT logicalrelid::regclass, partmethod, repmodel, colocationid,
       CASE WHEN partmethod = 'h' THEN column_to_column_name(logicalrelid, partkey) END AS key
FROM pg_dist_partition;
SELECT logicalrelid::regclass, count(*) FROM pg_dist_shard GROUP BY logicalrelid;
SQL

A one-task EXPLAIN alone does not prove hash distribution. Scope routing queries by userId; inspect catalog metadata to distinguish local/reference registrations from hash shards.

docs.title: CloudNativePG: physical replication
docs.text:
What is it? CNPG is a Kubernetes operator managing PostgreSQL primary/replica Pods and failover. PostgreSQL streams WAL (write-ahead log) to a standby.

Why Clichy uses it Dev/Production use its primary Service directly, while Test retains a separate CNPG cluster for replication exercises. CNPG does not replicate Test's Citus database.

flowchart LR
  App[Dev / Production application] --> RW[clichy-postgres-rw Service]
  RW --> Primary[Primary Pod and PVC]
  Primary -->|Asynchronous WAL streaming| Replica[Replica Pod and separate PVC]
  Operator[CNPG operator] -. reconciles and promotes .-> Primary
  Operator -. supervises .-> Replica

cnpg/cluster.yaml declares two PostgreSQL instances with preferred anti-affinity and asynchronous streaming (minSyncReplicas: 0, maxSyncReplicas: 0). Both run on the same host. Writes do not wait for standby acknowledgement, so failover can lose recent transactions. The operator updates the -rw Service after promotion; the app has no replica-read routing.

Check live roles using kubectl get pods -n clichy-prod -l cnpg.io/cluster=clichy-postgres -L cnpg.io/instanceRole. On the primary, SELECT application_name, state, sync_state FROM pg_stat_replication; shows senders. The Production healthcheck observes a streaming standby; neither that observation nor Ready status demonstrates failover or zero data loss. The optional kubectl cnpg status command requires a separate plugin.

docs.title: Backups and limits
docs.text: There is no tested backup/restore automation. Database replicas, Redis AOF and PV Retain do not protect against accidental deletion or loss of valtask. A verified backup must coordinate PostgreSQL metadata with original/derivative files and be restored into an isolated target. Do not delete PVCs, redistribute existing tables or resolve failed migrations blindly. Historical repairs remain available in Git history rather than in normal deployment manifests.

docs.title: Kubernetes and environments
docs.text:
What is it? Kubernetes schedules containers and manages Services, persistent volumes and workload controllers. K3s packages it for a small server with Traefik, local-path storage and Metrics Server.

Why Clichy uses it The same application manifests support namespace-specific configuration, rollouts and scaling on the intentionally single-node valtask.

docs.title: Environments and resources
docs.text:
Environment Namespace Application database Storage Dev clichy-dev CNPG Local-path; local cluster Test clichy-test Citus; separate CNPG exercise Local-path Production clichy-prod CNPG Retained local PVs on valtask

infra/kubernetes/base defines Web/API/worker, Redis, photo storage and Ingress. overlays/{dev,test,prod} customize hosts, image names, configuration and replica counts. Their database subdirectories configure CNPG; standalone Test Citus is in infra/kubernetes/citus. Separate namespaces and Secrets are logical isolation, not separate clusters or host-level availability.

docs.title: Prepare a server
docs.text:
These steps modify a host/cluster; review scripts before running them. No installation command is needed for normal local application development.

  1. Prepare Ubuntu Server 24.04 with hostname valtask, working SSH and a mounted /srv/clichy for Production. Install baseline tools using ordinary APT:
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install --no-install-recommends ca-certificates curl git gnupg jq openssl python3 tar ufw
  1. Configure Tailscale/MagicDNS and firewall policy. Verify tailscale ping valtask from an authorized client. Restrict ports 80, 3000 and 4466 to the intended private clients; existing UFW rules and SSH access require host-specific review.
  2. Run ./infra/kubernetes/scripts/install-k3s.sh as the non-root operator. It writes a mode-0600 kubeconfig, default ~/.kube/config-k3s; set KUBECONFIG to it explicitly and inspect kubectl get nodes. It does not alter firewall/SSH.
  3. Run ./infra/kubernetes/scripts/install-helm.sh if Helm is absent. Then run ./infra/kubernetes/cnpg/install-operator.sh before namespace preparation. The pinned K3s default is 1.37; the pinned CNPG installer treats that as tested but unsupported and requires the explicit CNPG_ALLOW_TESTED_UNSUPPORTED_K8S=1 acknowledgement. Do not silently bypass this check.
  4. Run ./infra/kubernetes/scripts/prepare-namespace.sh test (and prod when preparing Production). The script confirms the target, generates/reuses local mode-0600 secret files under ~/.config/clichy, normalizes the DB host/user, asks for GHCR read credentials, creates isolated Secrets and waits for databases.
  5. Install monitoring and optionally Headlamp with their scripts. Use configure-lan-access.sh for the Traefik admin ports; it refuses to overwrite conflicting Traefik values. See scripts.
  6. Configure the self-hosted runner, then deploy through CI.

Namespace preparation can change Secrets; it is not a routine healthcheck. Test uses clichy-server-secrets, Production clichy-prod-secrets; each namespace also has clichy-postgres-app and ghcr-pull-secret. Never display their data in logs or copy credentials between environments.

docs.title: Persistent storage
docs.text:
API and worker share the 10 GiB clichy-server-photos claim at /data/photos; Redis has a 1 GiB claim. Test Citus has its own claim. CNPG creates two separate 2 GiB claims per environment. Production pre-binds CNPG to local PVs under /srv/clichy/k3s-storage/prod/postgres-cnpg-{1,2}, with UID/GID 26, node affinity and Retain. Preparation refuses unsafe existing paths and requires the mount.

The old Production PostgreSQL PV/path remains reserved in the storage manifest; removing the unused old StatefulSet source does not delete that live volume. Do not delete/reuse it as part of normal deployment. ReadWriteOnce claims fit this one-node design; monitor actual disk use, not just declared PVC capacities. Retain, replicas and local-path storage are not backups.

The Dev overlay uses local :dev image tags; load locally built images into your chosen cluster yourself. The deploy.sh entry point is intentionally restricted to Test/Production on valtask.

docs.title: Portability
docs.text: A cloud move would retain application images and namespace isolation, but replace valtask-bound local PVs with provider storage and supply a shared photo volume accessible to API/worker. Review ingress/DNS/tunnel endpoints, Secrets, runner kubeconfig, node assumptions in deploy/migrate and CNPG storage classes together. Restore a coordinated backup into an isolated environment and validate before cutover. No cloud overlay or tested migration automation is provided.

docs.title: Redis and BullMQ
docs.text:
What is it? Redis stores in-memory data with optional persistence; BullMQ uses Redis to coordinate queued jobs, retries and worker delivery.

Why Clichy uses it Image processing runs outside the API request lifecycle. The PostgreSQL outbox keeps unpublished work durable when Redis is unavailable.

Each namespace has one Redis Deployment, AOF and a 1 GiB PVC, with noeviction and a 256 MiB memory budget. It is internal, not a replicated cache. Queue names/credentials must agree between API and worker. See the photo lifecycle for recovery and retry semantics.

docs.title: Prometheus and Grafana
docs.text:
What is it? Prometheus scrapes time-series metrics and evaluates rules; Grafana displays them. Exporters expose measurements; ServiceMonitor/PodMonitor resources tell Prometheus where to scrape.

Why Clichy uses it Operators need HTTP latency/error rate, queue backlog, worker failures, disk capacity and PostgreSQL replication visibility.

install-monitoring.sh installs the pinned kube-prometheus-stack chart into monitoring. Versioned Helm values, monitors, rules and the Clichy Photo Service dashboard live under infra/kubernetes/monitoring. The ordinary Test workflow applies monitoring manifests without upgrading Helm. Re-running the installer for an existing release requires a reviewed explicit upgrade.

Source Discovery and useful signals API /metrics ServiceMonitor; HTTP rate/status/duration and unpublished outbox Worker /metrics PodMonitor; BullMQ state, attempts, duration and query health CNPG metrics PodMonitor; PostgreSQL WAL/replication Node and Kubernetes exporters CPU/memory, PVC usage, Pod restarts and availability

Open private Grafana at http://valtask:3000, select the environment and inspect the dashboard. Verify Prometheus → Status → Targets before interpreting an empty panel as idle. Rules cover backlog, missing scrapes, unavailable workloads, restarts, resource pressure, storage and HPA limits. Retention is seven days. Headlamp at http://valtask:4466 is optional private cluster administration.

docs.title: HPA and Metrics Server
docs.text:
What is it? HPA adjusts Deployment replica counts from observed metrics. Metrics Server supplies the Kubernetes resource metrics API used for CPU scaling; Prometheus is a separate monitoring system.

Why Clichy uses it Test Web/API can scale from one to four replicas at 70% of requested CPU. Worker, Redis and databases do not have HPAs.

Verify kubectl top pods -n clichy-test and kubectl get hpa -n clichy-test before load testing. An <unknown> metric needs investigation, not more load. For a bounded, confirmed Test-only load demonstration:

./infra/kubernetes/scripts/load-test-test.sh server 300 32
# Or use web instead of server.
kubectl get hpa -n clichy-test -w

The generator uses unauthenticated reads (API 401 is expected), creates local load and a temporary port-forward, and never uploads data. Observe sampling delays and wait for scale-down afterwards. Do not manually scale HPA-controlled Deployments. For a manual worker demonstration use kubectl scale deployment/clichy-worker -n clichy-test --replicas=2, then restore --replicas=1; this changes cluster resource usage. Extra replicas on one node do not add physical capacity or node-level availability.

docs.title: Deployment and migrations
docs.text:
What is it? A deployment rolls out images; a migration evolves the database schema through ordered versioned SQL. They have separate failure modes.

Why Clichy uses it The checked-out migration source and published images must describe the same commit, and database changes must precede new code.

docs.title: Normal deployment
docs.text:
Pushes to master deploy Test after CI. Production requires a manual dispatch with deploy_prod=true and its GitHub environment protections. See CI/CD for runner prerequisites.

For an operator deployment, use a clean checkout matching already-published images, and review the context before confirming:

kubectl config current-context
./infra/kubernetes/scripts/deploy.sh test sha-<40-character-commit-sha>
# Production is a separate, explicitly confirmed operation:
./infra/kubernetes/scripts/deploy.sh prod sha-<40-character-commit-sha>

The script requires exactly one node named valtask, a valid SHA tag matching HEAD, ready CNPG and isolated namespace Secrets. Test also prepares/waits for Citus. Production checks Secret keys and the GHCR pull-secret type. It runs migrate.sh, renders exact-SHA Kustomize images, applies them, waits for Web/API/ worker rollouts and cleans temporary files. CI uses CLICHY_DEPLOY_CONFIRM=yes as explicit non-interactive confirmation; omit it for manual use.

Migration failure stops application deployment. Deployment failure is not an automatic rollback: old/new Pods may coexist and applied database changes remain. Use backward-compatible expand/contract migrations and investigate before retrying.

docs.title: Migration commands
docs.text:
Command Impact pnpm db:migrate Local prisma migrate dev; may create/apply SQL ./infra/kubernetes/scripts/migrate.sh test status Read-only Prisma diagnostic through a temporary local port-forward ./infra/kubernetes/scripts/migrate.sh prod status Same, against Production CNPG ./infra/kubernetes/scripts/migrate.sh test deploy Apply pending versioned migrations to Test ./infra/kubernetes/scripts/migrate.sh prod deploy Apply pending versioned migrations to Production

Prefer deploy.sh for a release so migration and image ordering remain coupled. The migration script verifies relevant source cleanliness, workflow SHA when present, valtask, the environment Service and database name. It reads that namespace's Secret without printing the URL, opens a loopback-only ephemeral port-forward, probes PostgreSQL, runs Prisma and cleans credentials/processes. The loopback forwarding connection explicitly disables TLS; it is not a public PostgreSQL listener. status can exit nonzero for pending/failed history.

Citus distribution is now part of migration history, not a second post-migration registration script. Existing correct shards/data are retained. A fresh Test volume gets the extension from its pinned image and distribution from migrations. Other database names skip the Citus migration; see databases. Never edit applied SQL, reset a deployed database, or mark an unexplained failed migration applied. The historical one-off resolve command was removed; resolve new incidents only after inspecting their actual state.

docs.title: Observe the result
docs.text:
Run the environment healthcheck, inspect workflow logs and perform a separate authenticated upload smoke test in Test if needed. The healthcheck does not validate end-to-end uploads or zero downtime.

The first Test rollout of this simplification removes obsolete SQL mounts and restarts the Citus Pod under its existing Recreate strategy. Its PVC is reused; there may be a short Test database interruption. Old generated ConfigMaps are not pruned automatically. The pending registration migration is a no-op for an already-correct layout and for non-Test databases; it is still recorded by Prisma. No manual repair or volume recreation is required.

docs.title: Scripts & Commands
docs.text:
What is it? These are the supported operational entry points and their side effects. Commands assume the repository root and an explicitly selected kubeconfig; scripts never make choosing the correct environment unnecessary.

Why Clichy uses it Routine observations, installation, deployment and load testing should have clear responsibilities and predictable impact.

docs.title: Public scripts
docs.text:
Paths below scripts/ are relative to infra/kubernetes/.

Script / command Purpose Environment Impact scripts/install-k3s.sh Install K3s; prepare operator kubeconfig New Ubuntu 24.04 host Changes host/services; confirms install scripts/install-helm.sh Install Helm with checked APT configuration Ubuntu/Debian Changes host packages; confirms cnpg/install-operator.sh Install pinned CNPG operator Cluster Applies CRDs/operator after compatibility checks scripts/prepare-namespace.sh dev\|test\|prod Prepare Secrets, storage paths and databases Local Dev / valtask Test/Prod Changes namespace and local secret files; confirms scripts/configure-lan-access.sh Set Traefik private admin entrypoints valtask Changes cluster networking; confirms, rejects conflicts scripts/install-monitoring.sh Install Prometheus/Grafana Cluster Helm/Secrets/manifests; confirms; existing release needs explicit upgrade flag scripts/install-headlamp.sh Install private Headlamp Cluster Helm/manifests/RBAC; confirms scripts/deploy.sh test\|prod sha-<40-hex> Migrate then roll out matching images Test/Prod Changes database/workloads; confirms scripts/migrate.sh test\|prod deploy Apply pending Prisma migrations Test/Prod Changes database scripts/migrate.sh test\|prod status Full Prisma history diagnostic Test/Prod Database reads; Secret access and temporary loopback port-forward scripts/healthcheck.sh test\|prod [--verbose] Observe environment invariants Test/Prod Read-only Kubernetes/SQL/HTTP/Redis observations scripts/load-test-test.sh server\|web 300 32 Bounded scaling demonstration Test only HTTP load and temporary port-forward; confirms pnpm --filter server backfill:photos Reschedule incomplete library processing Configured API environment Changes database/queue; build first; review target

Bash/Node test files are internal checks, not admin commands. Baseline host APT setup is documented directly in Kubernetes setup, without a separate wrapper. No active script performs the old empty-table repair.

docs.title: Healthchecks
docs.text:
./infra/kubernetes/scripts/healthcheck.sh test
./infra/kubernetes/scripts/healthcheck.sh prod
./infra/kubernetes/scripts/healthcheck.sh test --verbose

Requires Bash, kubectl and GNU timeout (Ubuntu coreutils). No local database client or pnpm is needed. Kubernetes read/exec permissions are required; Secrets and connection strings are not fetched. Use the checkout whose migration names you expect in the environment. The script keeps the current context unchanged.

Scope Checks Both Namespace access, Web/API/worker/Redis rollouts and available replicas, PVC binding and required claims, Redis PING, internal API Service HTTP, applied/unfinished migration names Test Citus rollout/connectivity, reference user table, hash(userId), 32 Photo/outbox shards, colocation, validated foreign keys and update/delete actions Production CNPG Ready, primary/replica identification, PostgreSQL connectivity and streaming standby; Citus explicitly skipped

Each kubectl operation is bounded by a 10-second request and 25-second outer limit; rollout/wait is 15 seconds. SQL forces read-only mode and a 10-second statement timeout. Total runtime is the sum of checks. Raw command errors are suppressed even in verbose mode to avoid disclosure; verbose prints target scope. For detailed investigation use troubleshooting.

Example (abbreviated, not a live observation):

PASS Kubernetes namespace access
PASS Citus reference table, hash(userId), 32 shards and colocation
WARN Migration checks compare names only; checksum drift requires Prisma migrate status
Summary: PASS=20 WARN=1 FAIL=0 SKIP=0

Exit 0: no failed checks (warnings/skips allowed). Exit 1: failed check or missing dependency. Exit 2: invalid arguments. Missing required components fail. Migration-name comparison does not prove checksum equality or detect all extra history; use migrate.sh <env> status for Prisma's full comparison.

Internal HTTP is called from an API Pod; deployment probes cover Web/worker. This does not test public ingress, authentication, uploads, storage writes or job completion. Test CNPG streaming remains a separate replication exercise. Healthchecks never apply resources, run migrations, delete data or repair state.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
What is it? Diagnostics collect evidence about an unhealthy component. Recovery changes state and must be planned from that evidence.

Why Clichy uses it A failed Pod, migration or queue should not lead to unrelated changes, discarded data or a retry of an obsolete incident repair.

Start with healthcheck.sh test|prod, then inspect only the affected namespace:

kubectl config current-context
kubectl get deployments,pods,services,pvc,ingress -n clichy-test -o wide
kubectl get events -n clichy-test --sort-by=.lastTimestamp
kubectl logs deployment/clichy-server -n clichy-test --tail=100
kubectl logs deployment/clichy-worker -n clichy-test --tail=100

These reads may contain user data in logs; redact before sharing. Replace the namespace deliberately for Production.

Symptom Investigate Local client/types missing pnpm install, pnpm db:generate, pnpm env:generate; verify Node/pnpm versions and environment schemas Local DB/Redis refused docker compose ps from packages/db; check 5432/6379 and the selected .env Login fails Auth URL, browser origin, secret length and cookies; API/Web host assumptions Pod/PVC Pending kubectl describe pod / pvc; StorageClass, free space, PV affinity, mounted paths and Production UID 26 ImagePullBackOff Exact SHA tag, image publication and namespace pull-secret presence/type; never print Secret values API database failure Test: Citus and clichy-citus-rw; Prod: CNPG Ready/primary and clichy-postgres-rw; inspect endpoints and run migration status Migration/layout failure Read migration error and current catalogs; no reset, drop, automatic redistribution or blind resolve Upload 400/413 Supported format, 20 MiB upload cap and 40-million-pixel decoder limit Photo remains PENDING/PROCESSING Worker /ready probe/logs, Redis, queue name, outbox rows, common storage; allow documented stale-recovery intervals Missing thumbnail Owner, completed state and same original/derivative filesystem for API/worker Empty Grafana panel Prometheus targets and ServiceMonitor/PodMonitor discovery before assuming no traffic HPA <unknown> kubectl top pods -n clichy-test, Metrics APIService, HPA events and CPU requests; Prometheus is separate Public/private URL unavailable DNS/Host header, tunnel for Prod, Traefik entrypoint/class, Service endpoints and firewall

For CNPG inspect kubectl describe cluster clichy-postgres -n clichy-prod and operator logs in cnpg-system. For Test Citus inspect its Deployment logs and the catalog queries. Never infer that Test CNPG's health proves Citus is healthy.

A missing streaming standby does not by itself justify deleting a Pod or PVC. An incorrect historical Citus registration needs an inspected data-preserving migration plan. The old empty-table repair and hard-coded Prisma resolve mode are removed; Git history retains their context. Do not revive them as a generic repair. Verify coordinated database/photo backups before any state-changing recovery. No tested turnkey restore or automatic rollback exists.

For runner failures, inspect its GitHub Online/Idle state and service logs (sudo journalctl -u 'actions.runner*' --since '30 minutes ago'), then verify its actual account can access the configured kubeconfig and tools.
